In the 1960s, [Eugene F. Lally](/wiki/Eugene_F._Lally "Eugene F. Lally") of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory was thinking about how to use a mosaic photo sensor to capture digital images. His idea was to take pictures of the planets and stars while travelling through space to give information about the astronauts' position.[[13]](#cite_note-Belbachir2009-13) As with [Texas Instruments](/wiki/Texas_Instruments "Texas Instruments") employee Willis Adcock's filmless camera (US patent 4,057,830) in 1972,[[14]](#cite_note-14) the technology had yet to catch up with the concept.

fanoutqa_017063.x:
Instagram :: User characteristics and behavior :: Users :: Demographics :: chunk_0032
As of 2014, Instagram's users are divided equally, with 50% iPhone owners and 50% Android owners. While Instagram has a neutral gender-bias format, 68% of Instagram users are female and 32% are male. Instagram's geographical use is shown to favor urban areas, as 17% of U.S. adults who live in urban areas use Instagram, while only 11% of adults in suburban and rural areas do so. While Instagram may appear to be one of the most widely used sites for photo sharing, only 7% of daily photo uploads, among the top four photo-sharing platforms, come from Instagram. Instagram has been proven to attract the younger generation, with 90% of its 150 million users under the age of 35. From June 2012 to June 2013, Instagram approximately doubled their number of users. With regards to income, 15% of U.S. Internet users who make less than $30,000 per year use Instagram, while 14% of those making $30,000 to $50,000 and 12% of users who make more than $50,000 per year do so.[[415]](#cite_note-416) With respect to the education demographic, respondents with some college education proved to be the most active on Instagram, with 23%. Following behind, college graduates consist of 18% and users with a high school diploma or less make up 15%. Among these Instagram users, 24% say they use the app several times a day.[[416]](#cite_note-417)

Deputy Prime Minister of Singapore :: History :: chunk_0001
The office of deputy prime minister is the second highest position in the [Cabinet of Singapore](/wiki/Cabinet_of_Singapore "Cabinet of Singapore"), typically held by senior ministers. At times, two individuals could serve simultaneously as deputy prime ministers. The officeholder is generally assigned specific duties by the prime minister, including deputising in the [Parliament of Singapore](/wiki/Parliament_of_Singapore "Parliament of Singapore"). Additionally, the deputy prime minister often acts as prime minister during periods when the latter is abroad, on leave or incapacitated.

Established in [1959](/wiki/1959_Singaporean_general_election "1959 Singaporean general election") with Singapore's attainment of [self-governance](/wiki/Self-governance_of_Singapore "Self-governance of Singapore") from the [British Empire](/wiki/British_Empire "British Empire"), the first deputy prime minister was appointed by [Yang di-Pertuan Negara](/wiki/Yang_di-Pertuan_Negara "Yang di-Pertuan Negara") [William Goode](/wiki/William_Goode_(colonial_administrator) "William Goode (colonial administrator)"). The position retained its title following Singapore's merger with the [Federation of Malaya](/wiki/Federation_of_Malaya "Federation of Malaya"), [Sarawak](/wiki/Crown_Colony_of_Sarawak "Crown Colony of Sarawak") and [North Borneo](/wiki/Crown_Colony_of_North_Borneo "Crown Colony of North Borneo") to form [Malaysia](/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), during which Singapore functioned as a [autonomous federated state](/wiki/State_of_Singapore_(Malaysia) "State of Singapore (Malaysia)") between 1963 and 1965. [Toh Chin Chye](/wiki/Toh_Chin_Chye "Toh Chin Chye") was the inaugural officeholder, serving from 1959 to 1968.[[1]](#cite_note-2) It was vacant from 1968 to 1973, when prime minister [Lee Kuan Yew](/wiki/Lee_Kuan_Yew "Lee Kuan Yew") did not pick a deputy for his [Third Cabinet](/wiki/Third_Lee_Kuan_Yew_Cabinet "Third Lee Kua

While many languages and [dialects](/wiki/Dialects "Dialects") are spoken in the United States, [English](/wiki/American_English "American English") is by far the most commonly spoken and written.[[431]](#cite_note-452) *[De facto](/wiki/De_facto "De facto")*, English is the [official language](/wiki/Official_language "Official language") of the United States, and in 2025, [Executive Order 14224](/wiki/Executive_Order_14224 "Executive Order 14224") declared English official.[[4]](#cite_note-EOWP-4) However, the U.S. has never had a statutory official language, as Congress has never passed a law to designate English as official for all three federal branches. Some laws, such as [U.S. naturalization requirements](/wiki/Naturalized_citizen_of_the_United_States "Naturalized citizen of the United States"), nonetheless standardize English. How I Met Your Mother :: Season synopses :: Season 1 :: chunk_0010
Main article: [*How I Met Your Mother* season 1](/wiki/How_I_Met_Your_Mother_season_1 "How I Met Your Mother season 1")

In 2030, [Ted Mosby](/wiki/Ted_Mosby "Ted Mosby") (voiced by [Bob Saget](/wiki/Bob_Saget "Bob Saget")) sits his children down to tell them the story of how he met their mother.

The series begins in September 2005 with Ted ([Josh Radnor](/wiki/Josh_Radnor "Josh Radnor")) as a single, 27-year-old architect living with his two best friends from his college years: [Marshall Eriksen](/wiki/Marshall_Eriksen "Marshall Eriksen") ([Jason Segel](/wiki/Jason_Segel "Jason Segel")), a law student, and [Lily Aldrin](/wiki/Lily_Aldrin "Lily Aldrin") ([Alyson Hannigan](/wiki/Alyson_Hannigan "Alyson Hannigan")), a [kindergarten](/wiki/Kindergarten "Kindergarten") teacher and an aspiring artist. Lily and Marshall have been dating for almost nine years when Marshall finally proposes. Their engagement causes Ted to think about marriage and finding his soul mate, much to the disgust of his self-appointed best friend [Barney Stinson](/wiki/Barney_Stinson "Barney Stinson") ([Neil Patrick Harris](/wiki/Neil_Patrick_Harris "Neil Patrick Harris")), whom he met in the restroom at a bar four years earlier. Barney is a serial [womanizer](/wiki/Womanizing "Womanizing") who concocts elaborate con games, usually involving costumes and fake identities, designed to bed women, only to lose interest in them immediately afterward.

Ted begins his search for his perfect soul mate and meets an ambitious young reporter from Canada, [Robin Scherbatsky](/wiki/Robin_Scherbatsky "Robin Scherbatsky") ([Cobie Smulders](/wiki/Cobie_Smulders "Cobie Smulders")), with whom he quickly falls in love. Robin, however, does not want to rush into a relationship and the two decide to be friends. Future Ted reveals that Robin is not the mother after referring to her as "[Aunt](/wiki/Fictive_kinship "Fictive kinship") Robin".

Slim narrowly eclipsed Gates to top the billionaire list for the first time. Slim saw his estimated worth surge $18.5 billion to $53.5 billion as shares of [America Movil](/wiki/America_Movil "America Movil") rose 35 percent. Gates' estimated wealth rose $13 billion to $53 billion, placing him second. Warren Buffett was third with $47 billion.[[42]](#cite_note-Forbes2010-42) [Christy Walton](/wiki/Christy_Walton "Christy Walton") was the highest-ranking woman, placing 12th overall, with an inherited fortune of $22.5 billion.[[43]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily2010-43) At age 25, Mark Zuckerberg continued to be the world's youngest self-made billionaire.[[11]](#cite_note-rferl2010-11) American [Isaac Perlmutter](/wiki/Isaac_Perlmutter "Isaac Perlmutter") was among the newcomers with an estimated fortune of $4 billion largely acquired in his sale of [Marvel Entertainment](/wiki/Marvel_Entertainment "Marvel Entertainment") to [Disney](/wiki/Disney "Disney").[[42]](#cite_note-Forbes2010-42)

A total of 1,011 people made the 2010 list. The United States accounted for 403 billionaires, followed by China with 89 and Russia with 62.[[43]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily2010-43) It was the first time China, while including Hong Kong, placed second.[[42]](#cite_note-Forbes2010-42) A total of 55 countries were represented on the 2010 list, including Finland and Pakistan which claimed their first billionaires.[[43]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily2010-43) Eighty-nine women made the list, but only 14 of them were self-made.[[43]](#cite_note-ChinaDaily2010-43) The combined net worth of the list was $3.6 trillion, up 50 percent from 2009's $2.4 trillion, while the average net worth was $3.5 billion.[[11]](#cite_note-rferl2010-11)

The Taj Mahal was commissioned by [Shah Jahan](/wiki/Shah_Jahan "Shah Jahan") in 1631, to be built in the memory of his wife [Mumtaz Mahal](/wiki/Mumtaz_Mahal "Mumtaz Mahal"), who died on 17 June that year while giving birth to their 14th child, [Gauhara Begum](/wiki/Gauhara_Begum "Gauhara Begum").[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsher1992210-13)[[14]](#cite_note-14) Construction started in 1632, and the mausoleum was completed in 1648, while the surrounding buildings and garden were finished five years later.[[15]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESarkar191930,_31-15)[[16]](#cite_note-Creation_History-16)

The imperial court documenting Shah Jahan's grief after the death of Mumtaz Mahal illustrates the love story held as the inspiration for the Taj Mahal.[[17]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEChaghtai193846-17) According to contemporary historians Muhammad Amin Qazvini, [Abdul Hamid Lahori](/wiki/Abdul_Hamid_Lahori "Abdul Hamid Lahori") and [Muhammad Saleh Kamboh](/wiki/Muhammad_Saleh_Kamboh "Muhammad Saleh Kamboh"), Shah Jahan did not show the same level of affection for others as he had shown Mumtaz while she was alive. After her death, he avoided royal affairs for a week due to his grief and gave up listening to music and lavish dressing for two years. Shah Jahan was enamoured by the beauty of the land at the south side of [Agra](/wiki/Agra "Agra") on which a mansion belonging to Raja [Jai Singh I](/wiki/Jai_Singh_I "Jai Singh I") stood.
